transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m here because, well, things at work have just been really getting to me lately. We got this new operations manager a little while ago, and they've just been... picking apart all the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. I've been a quality inspector for a long time, and I know what I'm doing, but now... I just can’t seem to leave work at work anymore. 

I come home completely wound up. I end up snapping at my husband over nothing, and then I lie awake at night just replaying every meeting, every little comment. And the worst part is, the next day, I go in and I start second-guessing these routine quality calls that I used to make without even thinking twice about it. It's just... it's really starting to wear me down.
Since these work problems began, have you been feeling persistently sad or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad, exactly. I'm just... stressed and frustrated. I still enjoy my weekends when I can actually get my mind off work, and I still like spending time with my husband when I'm not snapping at him. It's not a sadness, it's just this constant tension that I can't seem to shake off.
Aside from work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several other areas of your life?

No, not really. It's pretty much just work. I mean, my health is fine, money isn't an issue right now, and my marriage is good—aside from me being irritable lately. It really all just comes back to this situation with the new manager. That's what's taking up all my mental space.
When did these symptoms first begin in relation to the new manager starting?

I was doing fine before they started. The trouble really started building within a few weeks of him changing all our procedures. I'd say by the second month, I definitely knew my reactions to him were affecting me well beyond just the workday.
